Sciurotamias.distinguishing_notes: Co-occurs (China) with Dremomys, Callosciurus, Tamiops, Eutamias, Spermophilus, Marmota and flying squirrels. Allen 1940 key places Sciurotamias among squirrels with tail considerably more than half HB and untufted ears, separated from Dremomys by a low, not convex brain case and white/buffy (not red-marked) underparts; Rupestes (S. forresti) keyed by 4 upper cheek teeth and a pale lateral line. Allen also notes that Sciurotamias differs from Dremomys in possessing cheek pouches. (Allen's key threshold "head and body more than 190 mm" is contradicted by KV2013 measurements down to 172 mm.) vs Eutamias: unstriped back, no facial stripe pattern of chipmunks, larger (172-290 vs 120-168 mm HbL). vs Spermophilus/Marmota: long bushy tail (>= 1/2 HbL), long rostrum.

DEFINITION-SENSITIVE CODINGS: Callospermophilus and Ammospermophilus have pale (dorsolateral/lateral) stripes on the sides of the back but an unstriped mid-dorsum; coded dorsal_stripes=absent, flank_stripe=present per the brief's definition -- if the key's user might count dorsolateral stripes as "dorsal", treat dorsal_stripes as ambiguous for these two genera. Otospermophilus has middorsal darkening (called a "stripe along the back" for O. douglasii) -> both states. Eutamias/Neotamias incisors bear fine longitudinal striations (well-defined grooves in some species) -> both states; Marmota incisors "smoothly rounded" (Howell) vs "minutely fluted" (Allen) -> both. INFERENCES: patagium=absent is inferred from tribal membership (patagium unique to Pteromyini); ear_tufts=absent for Marmota, Cynomys and Xerospermophilus is inferred from ears described as concealed in fur / not extending beyond fur / a mere rim; Neotamias hairy soles and low-crowned molars are inferred from Howell 1929 ("feet ... as in Tamias"; "molariform teeth much as in Tamias"). Marmota cheek pouches are "rudimentary or absent" (vestigial in M. broweri) and are coded as both states.
